To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Hok mRNA is translationly inactive because of a secondary structure formed by the 3'-terminus of the mRNA, that this structure is a fold-back structure and that this structure prevents antisense RNA from binding to the mRNA.

(i) the Hok mRNA is very unstable and translationally inactive in plasmid-containing cells, and (ii) the 3'-region of the Hok mRNA encodes the structural element that prevents the mRNA from being translated and antisense RNA from binding.
the 3' end fbi element in the Hok mRNA is a structure that inhibits translation of the Hok protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of plasmid stabilization and the regulation of gene expression in plasmid free segregants.
the mechanism of post-segregional killing and the control of the hok gene.
the mechanism of post-segregional killing and the regulation of the hok/sok plasmid stabilization system of plasmids R1 and R100.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FBI structure is the key element of the post-segregational plasmid stabilization mechanism.
the hok/sok locus of plasmid RK2/R1 is a complex regulatory system, which ensures plasmid stability by the post-segregational elimination of plasmid-less cells.
the hok/sok plasmid stabilization system of plasmids R1 and F consists of two regulatory levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hok/sok plasmid stabilization system has evolved a very efficient mechanism of plasmid stabilization which relies on a very tight regulation of Hok mRNA translation.
Sok RNA controls hok translation indirectly, through the mok translatoric coupling, and directly, by inhibiting translation of full-length Hok mRNA.

Hok mRNA is translation-inactive in plasmid-carrying cells, whereas in plasmid segregants it is translation-competent, and that this regulation is mediated by Sok antisense RNA, which binds to the mok transl. initiation region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hok mRNA contains a 3'-terminal element, termed the fbi element, which is responsible for the inhibition of translation of the Hok mRNA.
the 3' end of Hok mRNA folds back and forms an FBI (fold-back inhibition) element.
the FBI element is a novel regulatory element which can be used to regulate translation and/or antisense RNA binding.
